support: It is hard to picture a happier mix-up than two boards hidden in plain sight on each other's lanes for four decades, with every driver arriving where they meant to go.
I laughed out loud when I read the council's notice, and again last week when Nora Hale of Lower Gate showed me her board hanging in her front hall, the word Upper facing the door.
WV12-P01.5.note: The author laughs twice and calls the swapped boards a happy mix-up; there is no longing, praise of craft, fault-finding or concern, and the literal reading of the 'happier mix-up' sentence is consistent with the rest.

support: I laughed out loud the first evening I saw it myself: a chimney that has burned nothing for eleven years, drawing a cloud of smoke down into itself.
Until they go, every clear evening the old chimney smokes in reverse over the schoolyard, and I stand at the gate grinning up at it.
WV12-P04.5.note: Read literally, the writer laughs out loud at the chimney and grins up at it every evening, delighted by the joke of a cold chimney that seems to smoke backwards; nothing the writer says expresses esteem, disapproval, sorrow or worry.
